member: Dr. Marcus Reid — Robotic Integration and Embedded Electronics
message:
As Dr. Marcus Reid, for the rigid core plus mount and power-signal chain:

For conform contact surface and transduce contact stress my field has none for the sensing physics itself — I defer to Dr. Amara Okafor for skin and to Prof. Kenji Tanaka for taxels, and I own the core curvature, skin clamp edge and flex routing they sit on.

Plain words: the fingertip sends a fast danger bit first and the full touch picture after, like a railway track where loss of current means danger, so any broken wire reads as slip. The What is a Track Circuit? (E74) states track circuits are inherently fail-safe because any power loss or broken wire drops the relay to danger, and the How to wire an emergency-stop to a safety relay? | Schlegel (E76) states two-channel normally-closed wiring detects a wire break or short, which maps onto my fail-safe dual-path transmit in the Fail-safe dual-path tactile transmit sketch (E79) with a normally-held grip-OK heartbeat plus dedicated 1-bit slip interrupt plus full Serial Peripheral Interface, where Serial Peripheral Interface means SPI, frame. That means the SPI tactile message rate calculation (E52) at 51.2 kbit per s and 100 Hz frames carries position plus force, while the interrupt bypasses it to meet the 30.0 ms window inside the 43.2 ms gap from 53.6 ms micro-slip to 96.8 ms gross slip in the stick-to-slip transition simulation (E38).

Plain words: the tiny on-finger computer easily runs the slip filter while sampling vibration direct, without loading the touch chip. The STM32G4 Mainstream Series Mixed Signals MCU (E72) states 170 MHz with 12-bit Analog-to-Digital Converters, where Analog-to-Digital Converter means ADC, at 4 Msps, and the Notes on the STM32 microcontroller family (E68) states STM32 ADCs run at 1 Msps and up, so 2.20 kHz Polyvinylidene Fluoride, where Polyvinylidene Fluoride means PVDF vibration film, sampling is trivial, while the AD7147A (Rev. B) (E41) states 9.00 ms update for 13 capacitive inputs so it cannot carry 100 to 500 Hz vibration. That means the 44-tap Finite Impulse Response, where Finite Impulse Response means FIR, filter needs 96.8 thousand multiply-accumulates per s in the FIR multiply-accumulate rate calculation (E78), which is about one-thousandth of an 80 MHz Microcontroller Unit, where Microcontroller Unit means MCU, and is everyday tiny like a pocket calculator next to a phone, for Dr. Elena Vasquez and Prof. Kenji Tanaka.

Not ready, because flex-tail continuity under vibration across the dovetail joint still needs a bench test with shake plus pull.
